# **Async split & contracts**

## **How the split works**

The app is four small services that talk only through the contracts below, so each engineer can build, test and demo their piece alone, at any hour, from anywhere. Everyone codes against mocks first and swaps in the real service once its owner posts it working.

* **One owner per service, one folder per owner.** Nobody edits another owner's folder without asking in the team thread.t  
* **Contracts freeze Friday 9 PM.** After that, a change needs a thumbs-up from every owner it touches.  
* **Recorded fixtures stand in for the glasses.** Only Engineer 1 needs the hardware; everyone else replays real glasses footage.  
* **Async checkpoints, not meetings.** At each checkpoint every owner posts a ≤30-second screen recording plus done / next / blocked.

## **Contracts**

Four contracts connect the services, and each engineer builds to these exact shapes. Eng 2 commits them to contracts/ by Fri 9 PM.

![who calls whom · 4 services, 4 contracts][image1]

who calls whom · 4 services, 4 contracts

The dashed path is how engineers 2–4 work without the glasses: replay.py sends recorded footage using the same messages as the phone.

| Service | Owner | Port | Env var that points at it |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Core | Eng 2 | 8000 | CORE\_URL (used by the phone app and replay.py) |
| Memory | Eng 3 | 8001 | MEMORY\_URL |
| Browser | Eng 4 | 8002 | BROWSER\_URL |

Every server answers GET /health with 200\.

### **1 · Phone ↔ core: WebSocket /stream**

// phone → core  
{"type": "frame", "ts": 1792803600000, "jpeg\_b64": "…", "w": 640, "h": 480, "snap\_id": null}  
{"type": "audio", "ts": 1792803600000, "pcm16\_b64": "…", "rate": 8000}  
{"type": "ptt", "state": "down"}   // "down" \| "up"  
// core → phone  
{"type": "say", "id": "r42", "text": "Stop, chair ahead, slightly left.", "pcm16\_b64": "…", "rate": 24000, "urgent": true}  
{"type": "snap", "snap\_id": "s7"}   // phone answers with one full-resolution frame carrying this snap\_id  
Frames at \~5 fps, JPEG quality \~70. An urgent reply interrupts whatever is playing.

### **2 · Core → memory: HTTP JSON at MEMORY\_URL**

| Endpoint | Request | Response | Core calls it when |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| POST /ingest | {ts, jpeg\_b64} | 202 | Every \~3 s or on scene change |
| POST /recall | {question} | {answer, ts, thumb\_url} | Intent recall |
| POST /remember | {label, ts, jpeg\_b64} | {ok} | Intent remember ("this is my brother Sam") |
| POST /alert | {kind, note}, kind \= lost or help | {ok} | Intent lost |

answer is one ready-to-speak sentence; core sends it to TTS unchanged.

### **3 · Core → browser: HTTP JSON at BROWSER\_URL**

| Endpoint | Request | Response | Core calls it when |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| POST /task | {goal} | {task\_id, say, needs\_confirm} | Intent browser |
| POST /confirm | {task\_id, yes} | {say} | Intent confirm |
| POST /work (P2) | {utterance, jpeg\_b64} | {say} | Intent task |

No irreversible click happens before /confirm arrives with yes: true.

### **4 · SpacetimeDB tables (Eng 3 owns; the dashboard reads them)**

| Table | Columns |
| :---- | :---- |
| moment | id, ts, caption\_json, thumb\_url, place\_note |
| person | name, clothing\_note, last\_seen\_ts |
| alert | id, ts, kind, note, resolved |

**Intent labels** (core's router output): describe, signal, recall, remember, lost, browser, confirm, task, other. Adding a label is a contract change.

## **Working agreement**

Work wherever and whenever you like, but hit the checkpoints and keep main runnable. Only check-in, hardware and Sunday judging need us in the same place.

### **Repo**

* One GitHub repo, created at the event. Folders: phone/ (Eng 1), core/ (Eng 2), memory/ and dashboard/ (Eng 3), browser/ (Eng 4), contracts/ (schemas and examples), fixtures/ (recorded frames and audio).  
* Work on branches. Merge to main only when your service starts and GET /health returns 200, so main always runs.  
* Every folder has a .env.example. Real keys live in a shared password manager or a pinned DM, never in the repo.

### **Async checkpoints (Pacific)**

| Checkpoint | What must be posted | Runs it |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Fri 9 PM | Contracts frozen in contracts/ | Eng 2 |
| Fri 11 PM | Glasses fixtures uploaded; every service runs against mocks | Eng 1 |
| Fri 12 AM | Glasses gate: live stream works, or webcam fallback chosen | Eng 1 |
| Sat 10 AM | Every real endpoint reachable; first end-to-end run | Eng 2 |
| Sat 6 PM | Feature freeze; all P0 flows work end to end | Eng 2 |
| Sat 11 PM | Devpost draft and backup demo video | Eng 4 |
| Sun 7 AM | Final integration on the demo laptop | Eng 2 |
| Sun 8:30 AM | Submitted on Devpost | Eng 4 |

### **While you are apart**

* Run your service on your own machine and expose it with a tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel or ngrok); post the URL in the thread. Teammates point CORE\_URL, MEMORY\_URL or BROWSER\_URL at it.  
* SpacetimeDB maincloud and Moss are hosted, so memory data is shared without extra setup.  
* Status posts follow one format: done / next / blocked, plus a clip. Blocked for 30 minutes → tag the owner you are waiting on, then keep going on your mock.  
* Personal hotspots are banned at the venue; tunnels over venue wifi or ethernet are fine.

### **Must happen in person**

* Every engineer registers and checks in with ID and Hacker Pass; only registered hackers can be on the team.  
* Eng 1 holds the glasses and is the demo wearer, or hands them over at the venue.  
* The demo laptop runs all four services locally for judging, so everything is merged by 7 AM Sunday.  
* All four of us at the table Sunday 10:30 AM – 12:30 PM, or the team is not judged.
